claims.text: Local lattice distortions quantified by mean-square atomic displacement (MSAD) govern low-temperature strength in equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-derived concentrated solid solutions.
Local lattice distortions create a spatially varying dislocation glide-resistance landscape.
Cr-containing or Cr-richer alloys have larger MSAD.
Alloys with higher MSAD have higher extrapolated 0 K CRSS.
Below room temperature, dislocation motion is thermally activated over solid-solution obstacles associated with local lattice distortions.
Cooling relative to room temperature substantially increases CRSS.
Dislocation inertia becomes significant below approximately 60–77 K.
Dislocation inertia causes the low-temperature CRSS increase to level off below about 77 K.
At elevated temperatures, Mn and Fe diffuse to form solute atmospheres around moving dislocations.
Mn- and Fe-rich solute atmospheres elastically and temporarily pin moving dislocations.
Dynamic solute pinning becomes significant around 673–873 K and above.
Dynamic solute pinning causes serrated plastic flow characteristic of Portevin–Le Chatelier behavior.
Dynamic solute pinning produces a modest high-temperature CRSS increase relative to an intermediate-temperature baseline.
Alloys with higher combined Mn and Fe content exhibit a larger serrated-flow strengthening increment.
The intermediate-temperature CRSS is nearly temperature-independent before the onset of Portevin–Le Chatelier behavior.
Extrapolated normalized strength τ0/μ should correlate with normalized lattice distortion sqrt(MSAD)/b.
Magnetic transitions may cause deviations from the proposed MSAD–CRSS relationship because nonmagnetic DFT does not capture them.
Suzuki segregation may make a minor contribution to the observed behavior.

contradictions.description: The prediction and mechanism state that CRSS should level off below about 77 K because of inertia, but the falsification rule says that leveling off below about 77 K is grounds for rejection.

The boundary restricts validity to temperatures above the 60–77 K inertial regime and only up to where dynamic pinning becomes significant, while the mechanism and predictions explicitly cover both the sub-77 K inertial regime and the high-temperature dynamic-pinning regime.
